newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. spot resids steady to up with crude.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. spot resids steady to up with crude.

text.p: Most U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to higher Monday in lackluster trade, again helped by a rally in crude and still-tight East Coast supplies, industry sources said.
"It looks like resid prices will at least hold through the month. There's not a lot of underlying demand, but there's still not a lot of supply," said one cash trader.
In New York Harbor, 0.3 percent low pour and high pour notionally remained firm, with LP gaining 50 cents to about $23.75 a barrel and HP up a quarter to about $22.75, traders said.
And with utilities reluctant to build stocks at current prices, some said a cold winter could trigger a sharp spike.
"If we get another severe winter, there may not be enough there," said another trader.
NYH physical one percent held steady at $20.75, with 50,000 barrels for October delivery done at $21.50 (delivered Mass.).
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent held steady at $19.75-20.00, while three percent edged up slightly to $19.75-20.00, traders said. No USG deals were reported.
New York City gate gas prices were steady to firmer Monday in the mid-$2.40s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at $3.29/mmBtu equivalent.
